_doc: Street look (render/roads): plate_tone_power is how fast an arm's asphalt gives way on a node's paving, off its mouth (render/roads/road_plate.cpp): each arm's colour is weighed by its carriageway's width over the distance to its mouth, to this power, so at 2 an avenue's asphalt runs through a junction and a side street's passes into it within its own throat; a modelling choice, no norm. strip colours (sRGB; over the grass map a tint, white for the map as it is); surface_colors[0] is the colour the asphalt texture is authored against, asphalt_by_class the tone over it, heights.skirt how far a road's outer faces reach down (the raised strips' heights over the carriageway are the catalogue's, tuning.json street, read by the simulation too), median_nose_m how far a median stands back of a crossing, verge the ground from a footway's edge down to reach_m out and under_m below the terrain, in that many strips, dropped kerbs, markings and how the street furniture looks (a junction corner's and a turning bulb's stations are the simulation's: tuning.json road, sim/roads/node_outline.h); where the furniture stands and where the crosswalk and stop line lie is data/catalog/street_furniture.json. markings follow CONTRAN's Manual Brasileiro de Sinalização de Trânsito, vol. IV, Sinalização Horizontal (2007): white N 9.5 and yellow 10YR 7.5/14 Munsell, as sRGB through the Munsell renotation data (RIT real.dat; Y by ASTM D1535; illuminant C to D65 by Bradford); longitudinal lines 0.10 m below 80 km/h and 0.15 m from it, an exclusive lane's line 0.25 m (its 0.20 to 0.30 m), double lines 0.10 m apart; dashes by speed, the first pattern its tables give for each band (below 60 km/h 2 m dash, 4 m gap; to 80, 3 and 6; beyond, 3 and 9); zebra bars 0.35 m wide 0.55 m apart, the middle of its 0.30 to 0.40 and 0.30 to 0.80 m, as many as fit across the carriageway and centred on it. The heights in tuning.json street: kerb, sidewalk and median 0.15 m over the carriageway (Porto Velho LC 748/2018 and the São Paulo standard kerb: 15 cm over the grade; the sidewalk level with the kerb's top), barrier 0.81 m (FHWA: the 32 in New Jersey safety shape). Dropped kerbs (ABNT NBR 9050): no lip at the road (low_m 0), the ramp across the footway and its far wing at most 1:12, 1.80 m for a 0.15 m kerb (run_m, flare_m); the wing on the junction side (full_m), where the ramp starts and ends along the kerb (flat_m) and the narrowest footway that gets one (min_walk_m) are not yet sized from the crosswalk (data/catalog/street_furniture.json crossing): the norm wants 1.20 m left free behind the ramp, else the whole footway lowered with 1:20 ramps along it.

markings._doc: styles: the regional paint standards of Menu > Paint (the order of the choices, the 4.0's ids), each with its dashes by speed and whether every line is white; a style's widths are base's unless it gives its own. br is the 4.0's drawing (markingStyle.ts 'br': dashes 3, 3, 4 m with gaps 6, 9, 12 m by speed, the style every new city of the 4.0 starts with, main.ts) and is the game's default: where the standard and the 4.0 differ in looks the 4.0 is drawn and the standard is a second table. br_norm is that second table, CONTRAN MBST vol. IV section 4.1 (dashes 2/4, 3/6 and 3/9 m, line widths of 0.10 m and 0.15 m from 80 km/h, double line on a road with more than one lane a direction, zebra of 0.35 m bars every 0.9 m); it comes last so the indexes of the other styles do not move. us and eu take the widths of base until their sources are read (MUTCD part 3; Vienna Convention 1968, EN 1436).

dropped_kerb._doc: At a crossing (flare_m, low_m, run_m, min_walk_m: the street's _doc). At a lot's car gate, a vehicle access (ABNT NBR 9050 as the municipal guides state it, the City of Sao Paulo's sidewalk guide): the kerb lowered over the gate's width to a lip of drive_low_m (the 5 cm step kept between the gutter and the kerb at a vehicle entry), its ramp kept in the service strip beside the kerb, drive_band_m wide (NBR 9050:2004's least service strip, 0.75 m; steeper than 1 in 12 is allowed there), the walking strip behind it left level; the kerb rises back to its full height over drive_flare_m along it either side of the gate (no published value: a modelling choice, the crossing's flare).

props._doc: Parts in local metres (+z faces the road or the arriving traffic, base at y = 0). shape box (min, max), cylinder (base, radius, height, segments) or blob (center, radius); glow 'night' lights the part at night. Signal lenses: lens 0/1/2 = the cars' red/amber/green (on both faces of the head), 3/4 = the walkers' stop/walk (their head faces -x, across the crosswalk; the cars' red and green). color is the lens lit as the screen shows it (render/tone_map.gd gives the radiance): the colour regions of road traffic signals (CIE, as tabled by Janoff, Transportation Research Record 1316, 1991, Table 1; EN 12368 Table 7 asks the same) lie outside what an sRGB screen shows for red and amber, so each is the brightest colour the Environment's ACES can show whose chromaticity is within one MacAdam step (0.0011 in CIE 1976 u'v', CIE TN 001:2014) of the nearest one it can show (red: 0.0377 from the region, the nearest 0.0366; amber: 0.0073, the nearest 0.0062); green the brightest inside its region. An unlit lens is that colour times lens_dim (sRGB), a dark filter lit by the scene: in full sun (daylight.json sun and ambient) it stays at least 16 times dimmer than the lens lit, the phantom signal class 5 of EN 12368 (ratios 21.2, 16.6 and 19.9). The signal head: three 12-inch sections (MUTCD 4D.07; 300 mm lenses, EN 12368 6.2), each housing 13.5 x 13.5 x 7.0 in (SWARCO McCain traffic signal housing sheet), two back to back for the two faces, its bottom 15 ft over the road (MUTCD 4D.15), red on top; each lens a dome 2.0 in proud of its door (Leotek IL6-P3 12-inch module), under a cap visor as deep as the lens is wide, 0.10 in thick (McCain visor sheet), dull black (MUTCD 4D.12). The walkers' head: two 8-inch sections (10 x 10 x 7.0 in, 200 mm lenses, domes 1.7 in, 8-inch visors), the upraised hand above the walking person (MUTCD 4E.04), its bottom at 8.5 ft, the middle of MUTCD 4E.05's 7 to 10 ft. Housings and visors black: linear albedo 0.05, a black-pigmented polymer (Physically Based, 'Toner (Black)'). The lenses are not in the post's mesh: each is drawn once, lit or not, by render/props/signal_lamps.h.

wires._doc: The wires of a span, on the seats of each pole (Roadcraft 4.0 world/utilities.ts primarySeats, secondarySeats, spanCarries): the three primary wires on the cross-arm's insulators, z_m along it from the mast toward the street on an urban pole (B1), the style's rural_z_m on a rural one (N1, across the crown), the wire i from the seat i of one pole to the seat i of the other; the two secondary wires on the urban pole's rack (S1), the style's secondary_z_m out from the mast, only between two urban poles. The style's y_m: the primary wires' height, then the secondary ones'. sag: share of the span, up to max_sag_m. radius_m: thicker than life so a cable reads at play zoom, as the 4.0 draws it. min_span_m, max_span_m: what is strung. near_chords and near_sides are the tube, far_chords and far_sides the coarse level. A chunk's wires stand wherever its poles stand and at one level, picked each frame (render/props/prop_renderer.cpp pick): the coarse one from where its own error (the chunk's deepest sag over far_chords squared, plus what far_sides leave of the round) is under render.detail_error_px on the frame's lens at the nearest point of the chunk (render/detail.h), the tube nearer; no distance is set here. Sag has no norm behind it: measured against the 4.0 in play.

wear._doc: Streets and footways that age with use (render/wear): the field's cell, how much a wheel and a foot leave on the cell under it each simulated second (share of full wear: a busy lane darkens in a few minutes of traffic), the track of a car between its wheels (a sedan's 1.78 m width less a 205 mm tyre, agents.json), how often a tile is sent and how many a frame, and the most a publication counts for (ticks stepped with no frame drawn leave no wear: an agent stands on one cell for one publication).

trees._doc: Trees (native/src/render/trees): the models are one unit tall and scaled to their height. Each key's origin is in the _doc of its block: atlas (_doc), species (_species_doc), placement (_doc). What has no published or measured value says so, as a modelling choice. The wind lives in materials.json (vegetation). The street trees stand where data/catalog/street_furniture.json places them.
trees._species_doc: Species models, all keys a share of the tree's height unless said. dark, lit, bark and bloom tones: mixed in linear and written sRGB; the palette of the 4.0 under the same light, checked on crowns photographed side by side (ports/landscape/report.md), a modelling choice. shade_bottom and heart_shade: how dark the crown heart is, low and whole, in linear. jitter 0: no measurement separates a face's random tone from the leaf cards over it, so faces differ only by their normal. palm (Syagrus romanzoffiana, Carvalho, Especies Arboreas Brasileiras vol. 2, Embrapa 2006): arched pinnate leaves up to 5 m long give fronds length 0.38-0.46 of a tree of about 11 m; fronds count 10 is the low end of the 10-25 leaves a crown of field guides; trunk rings 5 are tube sections for the lean; segments 6 keeps the sagitta of a 5 m arc bent 90 degrees under a pixel at 30 m. Modelling choices, no published or measured value, compared with the 4.0 in the same frame: fronds lift, droop_rad, spin, young_length, young_lift, young_droop_rad, young_turn, width, fold and young_fold; a crown's own dark and lit (the palm's crownshaft and nuts); trunk top, r0, r1, facets, lean, flare and flare_h; cone; limbs count, reach, rise and r; crowns center, radius, rough, subdiv, cards, card and taper; heart_shade and heart_share (the share of its full size a heart under cards is drawn at); crown_reach; cards_shadow (whether the cards throw the species' shadow: a palm's fronds do); bloom above; fronds young, rise, droop, young_length, young_rise, young_droop, width and fold. seed: the random stream, no meaning. block (the hedge: a clipped piece, tree_parts.cpp tree_block): size its length, height and depth, bevel the cut of its long top edges as a share of its depth, rough how far its faces move from flat, segments its faces along its length, cards and card its coat of leaves, spread over its faces by their area; its section is the hedge's the lots lay (0.7 m thick, a metre and more tall), so a piece stood as thick as the hedge (render/trees/garden_place.cpp) keeps about its own length; its faces are the hedge itself (heart_share 1) under a thin coat. A modelling choice, no published value. No width is written anywhere: how big a species draws is measured from its meshes when the kit builds it (render/trees/drawn_body.h).

pictures._doc: picture_shade: the light a crown keeps from its own shadow and its neighbours, which a picture cannot cast: tree pixels of the far views against the 4.0 in the same frame (ports/landscape/plan-trees.json). The far level (render/trees/tree_pictures.cpp): frames of each species drawn from these elevations of the view; picture_share the frame side over the tree height, so the widest crown fits; frame_px the size at which a tree is never magnified at the near level switch (245 m at 900 px and 55 degrees: about 40 px).

atlas._doc: Leaf atlas, drawn once at start (leaf_atlas.cpp). Modelling choices of a procedural texture, compared by eye with the leaf masses of the visual-target photos (records/vegetation-terrain/08_park_day.jpg); no published or measured value: px (texture side), leaves (leaves per tuft), leaf_len_px and leaf_wid_px (leaf size), spread and squash (tuft shape), heart_bias (leaves toward the tuft's middle), leaf_tone_min, lit_lift, rim and rim_share (leaf tones), leaflets, leaflet_px, leaflet_reach, leaflet_vary, leaflet_rise and leaflet_tilt (frond leaflets), rachis_px, rachis_tone and frond_tone_min (frond midrib and tone), seed (the random stream, no meaning).

placement._doc: Where trees grow (tree_place.cpp, tree_look.cpp). density = clamp((patch - mass_from) / mass_span) * mass_gain + slope_gain * clamp of the true gradient over slope_grade (read slope_probe_m either side) + eco_gain * the ecosystem's wood share + forest_gain * painted forest - density_floor; patch: value noise at patch_m weighted by patch_weight. Bands by density: inner over its `from`, edge over its own, open below; keep: chance a cell of grid_m, a lattice from the corner of each lattice_span_m square of land, holds a tree, ramped across the band, and lone: the open band's chance below its `from`. woods_per_ha: all chances scale so the land averages this many trees (eco_mean, the mean wood share on map 0, stands in for the ecosystem in that sum). size_m: a tree's size; height size * (open_tall + crowd_tall * crowd), width size * (open_wide - crowd_narrow * crowd) * (1 +- width_vary); crowd: neighbours within crowd_reach_m, weighed down to 0 at the reach, over crowd_full. lean edge_lean * (1 - crowd) * min(1, crowd * lean_rise), to the open side. All of the above are modelling choices checked against the 4.0 in the same frame (woods cover and crown size, ports/landscape/report.md). Measured or published: max_grade 0.75, no trees on escarpado relief, over 75 % (Embrapa, Sumula da X Reuniao Tecnica de Levantamento de Solos, 1979); tint_vary 0.15: spread of the median crown luminance over 8 crowns measured on 14_lake_near.jpg, CV 0.088 times sqrt 3 for a uniform draw; near_m 245: a 12 m tree then spans 42-70 px of 900 at the camera's 55-35 degrees of fov. Sizing and modelling choices, no published or measured value: fade_m, far_m, far_shadows, min_y_m, road_margin_m, lot_margin_m, park_m2_per_tree, park_edge_m, park_max, park_height_m, street_height_m, forest_gain, and the species shares of mix, park_mix and street_mix (broadleaf, broadleaf_tall, conifer, palm, ipe_yellow, ipe_pink, shrub).

barriers._doc: The barriers drawn (render/props/barrier_boxes.cpp): beam_section: a guardrail's W, [y, z] in the unit box of guard_beam_m by beam_thick_m; the form of a W-beam, drawn by eye (NBR 6971 is paid; the Roadcraft 4.0 draws a plain box of the same measures). each run cut into pieces of at most piece_m that step with the ground, sunk sink_m so a slope never shows under them. guard_step_m: NBR 6971 through DER-PR ES-OC 07/18, posts every 2.00 m. The other measures carry no norm and follow the Roadcraft 4.0 look, and so do finishes: colour, metalness and roughness of each material.

lamp_light._doc: A lamp's lens and the lit air under it. The light on the ground: the lamps nearest the eye a real light each (render/props/lamp_lights.h, its numbers in tuning.json render.lamp_*), every lit lamp a pool of its own (render/props/lamp_pools.h; its size is the catalogue's lamps.pool_*, data/catalog/street_furniture.json). beam_radius_m: the lit air under the lens in rain. lamp_* and column_*: height and reach of the lens on a utility pole and on a lighting column. pool_slab_m: how far over and under the street's top a pool lights what stands there (the ground it lies on and the feet of what stands on it, the kerb and a footway's step within it), a modelling choice, no norm.

signs._doc: The plates (render/props/street_signs.cpp, project/render/sign_sheet.gd). sheet_*, plate_cell_px: a layer of the pictures; the layers grow with what a city uses, 45 name plates or 32 plates each. sheet_round_s: the least time between two pictures read back from the viewport. A 0.5 m plate gets 256 px per metre, and the camera at its closest (view_half_min 0.8) shows 562 per metre on 900 lines. plates and drawings: by style. The round plates, the warnings and the name plates, and the picture of every plate (rims, words, the walker, the arrow), follow the Roadcraft 4.0 look: no norm was read for them. outline_points 0 is a rectangle; rotation the first corner, in turns. drawings: the picture of each type, in SignType order, in shares of the plate: rim a colour round the field, inner_share how far the field comes out, word_height and word_width the lettering's height and room, bar, slash and the walker in shares of its radius, arrow its tip, its base and its half height. word_bold: FontVariation.variation_embolden of the lettering.

styles._doc: What changes with a city's regional style (session-rules.md, section 10), laid over this table by DataTables: a block here replaces the same keys above, a list replaces the list. The drawings are the Roadcraft 4.0 look in both for now.

roadcraft._doc: What the Roadcraft 4.0 draws (src/render/signs.ts PLATE; src/world/utilities.ts and src/render/utilities.ts placePole: the urban and the rural pole, 8.5 m, made by tools/assets/make_pole_parts.py). The look of this style, not a norm.

pole_cast._doc: What a pole casts, by the distance from the eye to the nearest point of its chunk: nearer than from_m the whole pole (an insulator shows there); from there only its parts of least_m or longer, round ones of `segments` sides; nothing from end_m, where a pole or a bin is thinner than a texel of the far cascades, and the chunk's other furniture stops casting there too. One level at a time, picked each frame (render/props/prop_renderer.cpp pick).

brasil._doc: The pole: Neoenergia DIS-NOR-012 rev. 08, in the catalog's poles. CONTRAN MBST vol. I (2022) 3.7, recommended for town: stop, R-1, side 0.35 m, 0.845 m across, an octagon; yield, R-2, side 0.90 m; round plates 0.50 m. z_m is the plate centre: 3.11 puts the bottom edge 2.0 to 2.5 m up, here 2.1 m.

pole_cast._doc: What a pole casts, by the distance from the eye to the nearest point of its chunk: nearer than from_m the whole pole (an insulator shows there); from there only its parts of least_m or longer, round ones of `segments` sides; nothing from end_m, where a pole or a bin is thinner than a texel of the far cascades, and the chunk's other furniture stops casting there too. One level at a time, picked each frame (render/props/prop_renderer.cpp pick).

eua._doc: To fill from the MUTCD (FHWA) and the AASHTO Green Book.

europa._doc: To fill from the Vienna Convention on Road Signs and Signals (1968) and the European norms.
